name: query_panel_unit_projection
doc:
Native-callable: build the future trade panel unit projection for the
given instrument + selected trade unit + balance/price snapshot.

Returns `None` when the instrument is not TradFi or the user has not
selected the Lot unit — native then falls back to its existing
zhang/coin/usdt rendering. When `Some(_)`, every field is UI-ready and
native must render verbatim (no parsing, no recomposition).

Native is expected to call this query at the following moments:
- on entering the panel (initial render),
- when the user toggles the trade unit chip,
- when max-available updates push a new value,
- when the ticker last-price ticks (throttled),
- when the user types a new amount (estimated value re-render).

`max_buy_zhang` / `max_sell_zhang` are zhang (contracts) — Rust handles
the zhang→lot conversion using the instrument's `lot_size_std`.
`current_amount_lot` is the user's typed amount **already in Lot units**
(the panel input field's Lot-mode content). Empty string means "no
input yet" → estimated value falls back to the 1-lot canonical demo.

`long_order_size_zhang` / `short_order_size_zhang` are the
percent-applied order sizes in **zhang** (raw, not lot) — same as what
Native passes to `BalanceLoader.refreshOrderPxSize`. These drive the
`buy_cost_display` / `sell_cost_display` cost computation. Pass empty
strings to disable cost — Native then falls back to BE
`buyCost`/`sellCost` for the cost label.

`leverage` is a decimal string (e.g. "10"); empty disables cost.
`is_market_price_selected` is the user's market-price toggle (limit-style
strategies); when true Rust uses `ticker_price` instead of `last_price`
as the deal price (mirrors Native `MarginInfoHelper.selectPrice`).

name: create_confirm_interactor
doc:
Build a fresh [`PureSpotLimitConfirmInteractor`] populated from the
current state (via [`build_confirm_snapshot`]). The child carries a
`Weak<PureSpotLimitInteractor>` so its `confirm()` action can route
back through [`Self::proceed_after_confirm`].

Lifecycle:
1. The pre-check pipeline calls this when `is_order_confirm_open` is
true (see `pre_check_order`).
2. The interactor is stashed in `pending_confirm_interactor` and the
`ShowOrderConfirm` UxEvent is emitted.
3. Kotlin retrieves the child via
[`Self::take_pending_confirm_interactor`].
4. The child is alive as long as the BottomSheet holds it; once the
sheet dismisses, the last Arc drops and the child is freed.

Marked `#[uniffi::export]` so future callers (e.g. a future Kotlin
direct-invoke path that bypasses the event channel) can build a child
on demand. Stage-1 callers go through `pre_check_order`.

§J.2 parent factory: builds the render-ready snapshot from the current
frozen submit attempt and returns a child carrying only that attempt id.
The Kotlin host calls this after the existing price-relationship check (replacing the
legacy OKDialog confirm). Stop (TPSL) orders have NO PreCheck (A3) — there
is no PreCheck result param, unlike the trailing confirm.
Live decision-time read of the order double-confirm toggle. V1 reads
`getOrderRemindConfirm()` per order right before showing the confirm
(stop funnel `OkTradePresenter.makeOrderConfirm:594`), so
config-not-loaded behaves as OFF (`get_order_remind_confirm()`
default-false). Pure query (spec §C `is_*`): zero side effects. Kotlin
gates the confirm sheet on it right before `create_confirm_interactor`;

fields.name: max_amount_display
fields.doc:
Maximum amount formatted for display.

Phase 4.3 — dual scenario routes this through the Rust TradeConvertor
port (see `common::display::trade_display::format_max_amount_display`)
and emits a `DisplayString::TradingNumber { sign: None, symbol:
Some(target_unit), .. }` (USDT/USD for U mode; base coin for COIN mode;
"Zhang" for CONTRACT mode). Helper consumes Phase 4.0
`cached_ticker_price` for branches that need a conversion rate (linear-U,
inverse-COIN); when the ticker has not arrived yet it returns
`Placeholder` so the row reads "--" matching Native.
Single ALSO routes this through the TradeConvertor port (same chain as
dual, with its own ticker subscription — `single/interactor.rs`).
Margin / Coin / BorrowedCoin format via `common::display::spot_margin_display`
(`format_spot_amount_4dp` / `format_borrow_amount`). ContractExp /
AccountRiskComparison do not render this row.

`LeverInfoValue::Single` for every scenario except Margin, which emits
`DualUnit` ("base or quote") off the response's quote-side amount.

fields.name: margin_display
fields.doc:
Required margin formatted for display.

Phase 4.2 — dual scenario routes this through the Rust SizeConvertor
port (see `common::display::size_display::format_margin_display`) and
emits a `DisplayString::TradingNumber { sign: None, symbol:
Some(profit_symbol), .. }` (USDT for linear; settle ccy for inverse).
Single ALSO routes this through the SizeConvertor port (same as dual).
Margin formats via `spot_margin_display::format_margin_required`. Coin /
BorrowedCoin keep `Single` here, but the row is not rendered (mapper only
pushes the max-amount row). ContractExp / AccountRiskComparison omit it.

Margin emits `DualUnit` ("base or quote") off the response's
`quote_margin`; the quote-only fallback is how V1 renders "0 USDT" when
the base-side margin is empty.

fields.name: liq_px_display
fields.doc:
Liquidation price formatted for display.

Phase 4.1 — dual scenario routes this through the Rust
ChargeConvertor port (see
`common::display::charge_display::format_liq_px_display`) and emits a
`DisplayString::TradingNumber` (linear: no sign; inverse: fiat sign).
Single ALSO routes this through the ChargeConvertor port (same as dual).
Margin keeps `DisplayString::Simple` here, gated off by `show_liq_px`
(V1 margin has no liq row — pending L3 device confirm whether isolated
margin surfaces one). Coin / BorrowedCoin: Simple + not rendered.
ContractExp / AccountRiskComparison omit it.
